problems: The Gardener reads as a beret, sweater and trousers; the Weaver as a broad pullover with a tablet; the Apprentice as a visor, sweatshirt and backpack. Their names suggest the Future more strongly than their visible construction.

Gardener, Weaver and Apprentice converge into similar rectangular shirt-and-trouser silhouettes at stream scale. Small wrist devices, chest patches and hair additions are carrying too much of the differentiation.
Most occupational details face forward or sit beside the hands, where the elevated town camera will diminish them. Stronger shoulder, head and upper-back identifiers are needed.

The Administrator's white costume and constellation badge establish some rank, but ordinary hair and a narrow visor do not provide a grand top silhouette. The detached screens visually spill toward the envoy and have no visible attachment.
The envoy resembles a more elaborate local Courier. Its tiny repairs, orbital badge and finger strips will not establish a far-travelled android delegation at stream scale.

The Weaver's wide hips-bound upper torso reaches into the shoulder area. The Courier and envoy have rigid hip-mounted panels extending across the upper legs; these need articulation clearance rather than moving as solid slabs.
The Apprentice adds a custom hair block without hiding the original hair, producing an awkward protruding tuft rather than a controlled costume silhouette.

Fails the core test: three of the four everyday kits (Gardener, Memory Weaver, Canopy Apprentice) are 'today's clothes recoloured'. Each is a boxy sweatshirt, straight jeans-like trousers and chunky snow boots, and only the hair or hat changes. Nothing in the silhouette says 'future'. In bubble-gum pink and mint they read as pyjamas or a hoodie and jeans.

Colour: the large surfaces all use the 'shirt' role, which renders as saturated pink (not in the age palette of ivory, pale blue, lavender, slate, cyan, sage and sand) or mint. Because all four kits share that one colour mass, the crowd looks uniform. There is no ceramic, knit or textile material language at all.

Kits are not distinct at stream scale. Gardener, Weaver and Apprentice have the same torso box, same legs and same boots, and differ only by small head toppers (pancake beret, hair block plus bun, forehead band plus hair tuft). From 40 degrees above, the Weaver and the Apprentice both read as ordinary hair. Only the Courier's helmet separates its kit.

Gardener: the 'hat' is a flat cylinder plus a squashed sphere, which reads as a pink beret or shower cap, not a future garden hat. The 'asymmetric jacket' is a small loose pink square on the hips bone at [0.13,0.06,0.025] that sits over the left thigh like a floating sticker; it does not read as a jacket hem, and the thigh will push through it on the walk cycle. The seed capsule (0.17 sphere) is tiny and the same teal as the hand. The chest strip reads as a name badge.

Courier (android): the base hands are still skin (tan on one wearer, dark brown on the other) under ceramic elbow spheres, so the android has human hands. The wrap-tabard is not a tabard: it is a loose 0.31x0.28 pink plate floating at z 0.16 over the upper thighs (hips bone, y -0.055), offset and tilted, so it reads as a floating square and the legs will clip it when they swing. Below the waist it is jeans and boots, which reads as a person in a helmet, not an android courier.

Memory Weaver: nothing says 'weaver' or 'future'. It is a wide-shouldered sweater with a darker hem, a tiny sand badge on the chest and a small teal tablet in the hand. The cape is a flat slab behind the back that is invisible from the front and barely visible from above. The hair block plus bun is just hair.

Canopy Apprentice: the pale vertical 'accent' strip at hips [0.13,0.3,0.18] floats on the chest like a phone in a pocket. The light-grey waistband reads as a modern belt. The backpack and sage cylinder are hidden behind the shoulders and only peek out as a sliver. The hair tuft at [-0.11,0.37] looks like a stray cube stuck to the head. The forehead band reads as a sweatband.

Administrator: the insignia is the one strong, readable element. Otherwise the figure reads as a doctor in a white lab coat or a bulky white sweatshirt. It is the same height and outline as everyone else, the mantle stops at the hips, and there is no grand silhouette from above. The three panels all sit on one side and reach out to x 0.79 m, so in the render they overlap the leader's head. In a crowd they will land on neighbours, and at stream scale they are three postage stamps. The flat hair-coloured block on top reads as a haircut, not office.

Envoy leader: does not read as 'from far away'. Torso in the shirt role is the same pink as the Gardener's and the Courier's, with straight trousers and boots. The long cape is invisible from the front. The 'layered tabard' is a loose light-pink plate floating over the thighs (hips bone, y -0.12, h 0.32), which clips on the walk. The meteorite token is two little cones under the left hand that read as a bell. The orbital emblem is a small dark square that reads as a pocket. The red repair patch is about 9 cm.

Envoy fit bug: the faceplate box is 0.24 wide at x -0.045 and the ivory side plate stops at y 0.26, so the skin of the base head shows at the upper right corner of the head (visible tan block). The android has a patch of human skin on its skull.

Readability from above: the only big shapes seen from a 40 degree camera are heads and shoulders. Apart from the Courier helmet, no kit has headgear, a collar, a hood or a held object big enough to carry the silhouette. Capes and backpacks are thin slabs at the back.
fix:
Seed-Capsule Gardener: Replace the beret and sweater outline with a fitted segmented cultivation smock, a raised neck seal and two large seed capsules physically mounted high on the upper back. Let the rounded capsules break the shoulder silhouette from above. Enlarge the forearm capsule into a clearly attached cuff; keep its light inset broad rather than adding tiny markings. Ceramic Wrap-Tabard Courier: Retain the ceramic helmet and diagonal chest band. Give the helmet a deliberate stepped rear housing, and make the parcel a chunky hard-shell container with one broad contrasting stripe and a visible grip. Shorten the central hip flap to clear the thighs, or split its lower section into separate leg-bound panels. Habitat Memory Weaver: Narrow the central upper torso from 0.62 to roughly 0.48 and move shoulder extensions onto their respective arm bones. Replace the plain cape slab with a short, stepped data-mantle attached at the upper back, using two broad contrasting surfaces readable from above. Make the wrist device a substantial fitted interface, not the primary role identifier. Canopy Apprentice: Remove the ordinary visor-and-sweatshirt treatment. Use a cropped fitted utility shell and a folded canopy assembly attached to the backpack, rising above one shoulder with a clear hinge and broad accent face. Hide the original hair if retaining custom hair geometry. Administrator of the Shared Constellation: Keep the white ceremonial mass and constellation disc. Add a substantial three-node headframe attached at the temples and rear collar, and repeat the constellation geometry across the upper shoulders. Introduce a dark collar and broad cyan upper-cape border for separation. Replace the three detached screens with one larger console visibly mounted to an articulated shoulder bracket. Far-Orbit Patched-Tabard Envoy: Establish an unmistakable machine body with a fitted asymmetric ceramic skull, dark mechanical neck and elbow joints, and solid mechanical hand shells. Use a fixed foreign plum-and-ochre panel scheme rather than the local shirt palette. Enlarge the orbital insignia onto a shoulder or upper-back plate and consolidate tiny repairs into one bold replacement panel. Split the lower tabard for leg clearance. Test every kit walking and turning at the actual 40-degree stream camera and thumbnail size. / GLOBAL: Build the future silhouette from shapes, not tints. Use fixed palette materials for the structural shells and big panels: ceramic #f1e9e5 / #d7e1e8, slate #36495e, sage #c6d6b3 / #739d97, lavender #c1b5dc / #8c80b4, sand #bca783. Keep the shirt/pants/accent roles for one personal panel or trim per kit, so pink and mint stop being the whole figure. Every kit needs ONE big readable silhouette feature that differs from the others: a disc hat, a helmet with a fin, a high funnel collar with a hood, and a sprout backpack. Delete every loose rectangle on the hips bone that floats over the thighs. Lower garments are either a full skirt or tunic box wrapping the hips (about [0.50,0.36,0.32] at [0,-0.08,0], flush with the body, never a thin offset plate) or nothing.

SEED-CAPSULE GARDENER: replace the beret with a wide, shallow sage sun-disc hat (head cylinder [0,0.34,0] size [0.62,0.04,0.62], plus a crown cylinder [0.30,0.08,0.30] in #739d97) so it reads as a disc from above. Make the asymmetric jacket real: a ribbed knit jacket box on hips [0,0.33,0] size [0.50,0.50,0.32] in the shirt role; one longer side panel on hips at [-0.13,0.05,0] size [0.24,0.22,0.33] that wraps the hip, not floating in front; and a diagonal closure strip in sand. Soft knee boots in sage (#c6d6b3) on each leg at [0,-0.62,0.02] size [0.22,0.36,0.24]. Make the seed capsule a 0.22 translucent-teal (#66f2df-tinted #55abc7) sphere held at [0,-0.52,0.08], with a small sage cone sprout on top, clearly larger than the hand.

CERAMIC WRAP-TABARD COURIER: keep the ceramic helmet and visor, but add a tall vertical fin (head box [0,0.40,-0.02] size [0.05,0.14,0.26], #d7e1e8) so it reads from above. Cover both hands with ceramic gauntlets (armL/armR box [0,-0.46,0.005] size [0.145,0.15,0.155], #f1e9e5). Add ceramic shoulder domes (sphere [0,-0.02,0] size 0.21, #f1e9e5) and knee discs on the legs (cylinder rotated x 1.57 at [0,-0.38,0.1], size [0.14,0.03,0.14]). Rebuild the tabard as a cloth panel that hangs flush from the shoulders: front on hips at [0,0.18,0.16], size [0.34,0.80,0.03], in the shirt role, with a matching back panel on the cape bone. Keep the diagonal sash. Make the legs ceramic (#d7e1e8 shins) instead of jean blue. Enlarge the parcel to about 0.26 and put it in the slate/cyan palette.

HABITAT MEMORY WEAVER (make this the elder): add a high stiff funnel collar around the neck on hips: 4 boxes forming a ring at y 0.66, outer size about 0.46x0.18x0.36, in lavender #c1b5dc. Add a soft hood falling back behind the head (head box [0,0.24,-0.17] size [0.34,0.30,0.10]) in place of the hair block plus bun, and hide hair. Give a long wrap robe to below the knee: hips skirt box [0,-0.22,0] size [0.50,0.60,0.33] in the shirt:dark role, plus a diagonal draped shawl panel across the chest in sage. The held object is a visible 'memory loom', a 0.34x0.26 lavender frame (four thin boxes) with three cyan threads, held in front at about 0.5 m.

CANOPY APPRENTICE (the young one): delete the floating chest strip and the hair tuft. Give a cropped puffy vest (hips box [0,0.40,0] size [0.54,0.36,0.36], accent role) over a sage knit. Use knee-length wide shorts (hips [0,-0.10,0] size [0.50,0.30,0.32]) with hide 'trousers', plus high sage socks and soft boots. Put a tall backpack on the cape bone ([0,-0.15,-0.08] size [0.32,0.42,0.18], slate) with a sapling sticking up above the shoulder (#739d97 cone at [0.12,0.25,-0.08] size [0.14,0.28,0.14]), so the sprout is the silhouette from above. Replace the sweatband with a short-brim soft cap (sand) worn backwards.

ADMINISTRATOR (head): make the mantle grand. Use a floor-length ivory coat (hips skirt box [0,-0.28,0] size [0.52,0.80,0.34], #f1e9e5, slate hem band) and a tall standing collar that rises behind the head (hips box [0,0.80,-0.12] size [0.50,0.32,0.06] with a slate edge), so the outline is taller and broader than anyone else's. Pull the three panels in and make them symmetric: one above-left [0.36,0.95,-0.05], one above-right [-0.36,0.95,-0.05] and one centred above and behind the head [0,1.12,-0.12]. Each is about 0.28x0.20 in lavender with a cyan screen, with thin cyan link bars between them, so the constellation reads as one halo-like symbol of office and never passes x ±0.45. Replace the hair cap with a sleek slate skullcap band. Keep the insignia as is.

FAR-ORBIT ENVOY (leader): fix the skin leak by making the base faceplate full size (head box [0,0.16,0.01] size [0.33,0.34,0.31], #d7e1e8), with the asymmetric ivory plate as a raised overlay on one side and a single swept antenna fin. Replace the pink torso with a weathered travel cloak: a wide hooded mantle over the shoulders (hips box [0,0.56,0] size [0.66,0.16,0.40]) plus side drapes to the knee, in slate #36495e. Put the layered tabard in sand and lavender, flush to the body, not floating over the thighs. Make the repaired right pauldron big (0.24 ivory box) with a bold red strap and sand rivets. Add a tall navigation staff to the right hand: a cylinder from about y +0.6 to -1.1 in the arm frame, in slate, topped with the faceted amber meteorite (two cones, about 0.20). Move the orbital emblem to the chest centre as a 0.22 slate disc with a thin rotated cyan ring around it. The leader should be the only figure with a staff and a hooded cloak, readable from across the river.
